## CEO BRIEFING

Dana, here's the state of play for your board call:

- **What happened:** At 11:42 UTC, we detected elevated error rates (502s) on the Batch API, affecting a subset of customers. The issue was isolated to one of our internal worker fleets (fleet-a). We have not yet confirmed the root cause, but we have two leading hypotheses: a change in database connection pool settings from a release earlier this morning, and a spike in load from one customer's large scheduled job. Both are under investigation.
- **Who is hit:** Seven customer accounts experienced failures, all on the affected fleet. We have their specific impact numbers. Contoso is one of them and has already contacted us about SLA credits; we are handling that.
- **What we did:** At 12:58, we mitigated by moving all Batch API traffic to the healthy fleet (fleet-b). Error rates dropped to near baseline (0.4% vs. 0.2% baseline) within two minutes. We are now in a verification window that closes at 14:30. We are also re-driving failed jobs for affected accounts; about 60% complete with no failures.
- **Current status:** Service is recovering, but we are not calling it resolved until the verification window closes clean. Root cause is not yet established. We expect to have more clarity after 14:30.
- **What to say:** If asked, you can say: "We experienced an incident on our Batch API this morning, affecting a small number of customers. We have mitigated the impact and are monitoring recovery. We are investigating the root cause and will provide further updates. We are also addressing customer concerns, including SLA questions."

We will provide you with an update after the verification window closes.

## ENGINEERING UPDATE

Handoff for the engineering team:

**Current status (14:20 UTC):**
- Incident INC-2026-1109-01 is OPEN, mitigated, verification in progress.
- Mitigation applied at 12:58: all Batch API traffic moved to fleet-b; fleet-a drained and out of rotation.
- Error rate on POST /v1/batch/jobs is 0.3% (baseline 0.2%). Verification window closes at 14:30.
- Re-drive of failed jobs is ~60% complete, no failures on re-drive.

**What's done:**
- Confirmed errors confined to fleet-a; fleet-b healthy.
- Ruled out upstream object-storage provider (status green, Files API healthy).
- Published status page updates (though the 12:05 update was premature; we've corrected course).

**Open items:**
- Root cause not established. Two hypotheses:
  - H1: Connection-pool change in `batch-api@2026.11.09-r3` (max pool size 80→24) shipped 11:31. Correlation noted, not tested.
  - H2: Concentrated load on fleet-a (3x average from 11:38, driven by wonka-industries). Untested.
  - They may interact, but no tests run.
- Rollback test for r3 has not been run.
- fleet-a still out of rotation; not returned to service.
- Re-drive not finished.
- Verification window not yet closed.

**Next steps:**
- Wait for verification window to close at 14:30. If error rate remains normal, we can declare resolved.
- After that, we need to test hypotheses: likely run a rollback test on fleet-a (or a controlled experiment) to see if pool change is responsible.
- Complete re-drive of failed jobs.
- Return fleet-a to rotation once root cause is understood and fixed.
- Note: SEC-411 (unrelated) – batch worker DB role has write access to billing schema; Marcus owns ticket, target this week.

**Communication:**
- No external communication about cause until confirmed. Ruth will only use approved list.

## CUSTOMER EMAIL

Subject: Update on Batch API incident and your account

Dear Contoso,

We are writing to acknowledge the issues you experienced with the Batch API this morning. We understand that you encountered elevated error rates on batch submissions, and we apologize for the disruption.

Your account (contoso) was affected between 11:43 and 12:56 UTC. During that window, you made 9,400 Batch API requests, of which 3,410 returned errors (a failure rate of approximately 36%). We have since applied a mitigation to redirect traffic to healthy infrastructure, and error rates have returned to near normal. We are monitoring the situation closely and will confirm recovery once our verification window closes at 14:30 UTC.

We are also re-driving the failed jobs from the incident window for affected accounts, and we will notify you once that is complete.

Regarding your question about service credits under Schedule B: Monthly Availability is calculated at the end of the calendar month based on all eligible requests across the Covered Services. We cannot confirm at this time whether the 99.9% commitment will be breached, as we need to assess the full month's data. We will provide you with the calculated Monthly Availability figure within 10 business days of month end, as per the contract, and if a credit is applicable, we will detail it at that time.

We will provide a further update by 15:00 UTC today. If you have any immediate concerns, please contact our support team.

Sincerely,
Northstar Support

## STATUS PAGE UPDATE

We are continuing to investigate elevated error rates on the Batch API. We have applied a mitigation to redirect traffic, and we are seeing recovery. Error rates are returning to normal. We are monitoring the situation and will provide an update by 15:00 UTC.

We apologize for the inconvenience.
